scope: Minimal process-monitor recovery delta: incomplete observations, bounded resampling, first failure/cleanup, and the early monitor preflight. No broad QA redesign or native execution.

resolvedItems.evidence: parse_group_activity marks matching-group rows with missing/unknown columns, PID, RSS, CPU or state as incomplete. Such rows are not numerically summed. An incomplete sample reports rssMiB/cpuSeconds=null and separately names measured lower bounds. A group with no observed rows is incomplete.

A Darwin ? or ?E state becomes state-unavailable rather than a fatal parser-format exception or a valid zero measurement. This is consistent with Apple ps tasks.c's unknown-state initialization and early information-query failures. It is a supported failure hypothesis, not a reconstruction of the lost failed row.

group_activity performs at most three snapshots with at most two 0.25-second inter-snapshot delays. Each ps command retains a three-second subprocess timeout. Recovery history is preserved in bounded partialSamples and up to 16 runner monitorDiagnostics entries.

Runner.run checks sampleComplete before using RSS totals or ProgressWatch. A still-live leader after unsuccessful resampling produces monitor-unavailable; the first failure is fixed before finally cleanup. If the leader exited during observation, the existing owned-group completion/cleanup checks still apply. The regression exercises a real portable Python child and confirms failure preservation and owned-group reclamation.

The inline preflight now requires at least one recorded lastActivity.sampleComplete=true before status can become passed. A no-record/quick Runner result creates a fixed monitor-preflight-no-complete-sample first failure and fails. A new guard executes the actual extracted inline script with the no-record Runner stub and verifies the failed proof.

The monitor churn probe is after the immutable helper fixture checkout and before Runtime source checkout, SDK acquisition or toolchain materialization. It uses an owned short-lived Python/sh/sleep process group, existing read-only permissions and no extra CI job. pipeline.py requires the successful preflight proof in its final completeness gate.
The plan retains both prior failures: run 39016143725 KeyError/configure and run 39018277446 process-activity-format/tools-materialize. The actual lost monitor field remains UNKNOWN_NOT_RECORDED.

preservedControls: Runtime source, SDK/toolchain/native harness pins and first-cause patch are unchanged.
Authentication conditions, native functional timeouts, sandbox/OS protection assertions, trusted native input and product qualification boundaries are unchanged.
CPU-active quiet linking and cumulative I/O continue to count as progress. No restored 195/210-minute human elapsed cutoff.
One standard macos-15-intel job, platform limit 360 minutes, initial exact-branch push/attempt 1, read-only contents/actions permissions.
No new Actions artifacts/cache uploads, product signing/publication/merge, new credentials or OS permission changes.
Only measured complete samples reach memory/stall decisions; incomplete observations cannot become proof of a safe zero total.

sourceEvidence.supports: Unknown state is a supported observation failure; current public source does not identify the exact runner ps binary.
State and numeric fields come from separate process/task structures, so printed zero values accompanying an unknown state cannot be assumed to be measured zeros.

limitations: The failed run's exact raw field was not retained; the ?/?E explanation remains a source-backed hypothesis.
Portable mocked-format and child-process regression checks do not prove Darwin ps behavior. The final early preflight must obtain an actual complete sample on the selected Mac runner.
The final immutable fixture, rendered caller bytes/provider readback and fresh trigger/ref preflight remain separate steps before any authorized activation.
No actual host TU, XUL build or native authentication has been executed by this review. Original timeout cause remains UNKNOWN and product qualification is false.
The preflight proves a bounded observed interval; it does not guarantee that a later process-information query cannot become unavailable. Persistent later monitoring failure still stops the run.
